conviction_note: The release's one new number is NAV per share at 31 July 2026, set against 1009.9p at 31 January. H1 paid out 36.29p a share in dividends, Pantheon's own revenue budget was quietly cut and its valuation has sat at £275m since June 2025, and the only offset is a small FX translation gain. So NAV per share probably comes out flat to slightly down, while total shareholder return stays positive. On a 34% discount to NAV, with the last two half-year results moving the stock +0.9% each, that is a mild negative lean (p_up 45) on a modest scale (abs 3.0). The findings sum to -0.35, which matches the scaled -0.3 in sign and size.

findings.finding: Pantheon is the largest holding: £106.99m at 31 Jan 2026, about 30% of NAV, on an implied £275m equity value that has not moved since the June 2025 purchase. Between the 2 Apr 2026 RNS ('approaching £30m' FY26 revenue, PBT 'in excess of £15m') and the 22 Sep trading update ('budgeted to approach £27.7m', PBT not mentioned), its revenue budget was cut by about 8%. So the HY NAV probably carries no Pantheon uplift, and possibly a mark-down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAV prints have moved BPM little: HY results +0.88% (2024-10-23) and +0.90% (2025-10-21), FY results +2.22% (2026-05-27). The FY25 jump (+42% NAV, largely Pantheon/XPT/ATC unrealised gains) came out at 2.07%. The 22 Sep trading update that carried the lower budget: -1.2% on the day, then about -3% over the following week (665 -> 645).
findings.original_quote: Revenue is budgeted to approach £27.7m in the 2026 financial year, up from c.£23.8m in 2025. (vs 2 Apr 2026: 'Revenue growth from c.£23.8m in the 2025 Financial Year to approaching £30m for the 2026 Financial Year' and 'Profit before tax budgeted to be in excess of £15m')
findings.why_not_priced: Neither release sets the two budget figures side by side, and no press coverage compared them. The valuation consequence is not public until the HY NAV. If the market had priced a Pantheon mark-down, the post-update dip would have held; instead the stock fully recovered to 669 (from 645).
findings.independence: April RNS with the higher budget: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/b-p-marsh-partners--bpm/follow-on-equity-purchase-in-pantheon/9504575 ; the flat £275m valuation in June 2025: https://insurance-edge.net/2025/06/30/b-p-marsh-ups-stake-in-pantheon-by-extra-2/ ; the soft market (Marsh index Q2 2026, property -12%), quoted in the same trading update

findings.finding: H1 paid out £13.0m of dividends (36.29p a share, including a 22.33p special), against undiluted NAV per share of 1009.9p. Unrealised gains of about £14m are needed just to hold NAV per share flat, so a headline NAV per share below 1009.9p is plausible even with positive total shareholder return.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In H1 FY26 the company paid £8.0m of dividends, NAV still grew 7.1%, and the stock moved +0.9%. There is no precedent here for a HY NAV per share decline.
findings.why_not_priced: The dividends are public and the arithmetic is mechanical, so most of this is priced. What is not priced is how a 'NAV per share down' headline reads to retail holders of an AIM stock with one analyst. Kept small for that reason.
findings.independence: none. Same document as the Pantheon finding, but a different fact (the cash distributions).

findings.finding: Sterling weakened over the period, GBP/USD 1.381 -> 1.346 (-2.5%) and GBP/AUD 1.959 -> 1.916 (-2.2%), between 30 Jan and 30 Jul 2026. That gives a translation gain on XPT (£64.03m, USD) and ATC (£37.68m, AUD) of about £2.4m, roughly 0.7% of NAV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate history. FX is a line inside the NAV bridge.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and mechanical, and nobody publishes a NAV forecast for this one-analyst name. Partly offsets the Pantheon finding.

findings.finding: ATC (27%, £37.68m) closed its London expansion via the Frontier Global / Bastion acquisition in May 2026 and was budgeting more than US$300m of GWP for its year to 30 June 2026. That year-end falls inside BPM's half, so ATC's year-end numbers feed the HY mark, with a modest upside bias.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In FY25, unrealised gains on Pantheon, XPT and ATC totalled £81.8m, and the FY results day moved +2.07%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference about a private-company mark that nobody forecasts publicly. It is a proxy, so it is kept small.

findings.finding: Founder Brian Marsh, now Life President rather than a director, cut his holding from 39.25% to 38.51% (265,000 shares, about £1.7m) on 5 Oct 2026, inside the 30 days before the HY results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There was a 2025 phased secondary placing by the founder and the stock absorbed it. Since this disclosure the price has risen from 649 to 669.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed 12 days ago and the price has since gone up, so it is mostly priced. What remains is a signal from the largest holder about timing.

findings.finding: The buyback is still running. A programme launched 8 July 2026 had repurchased 120,000 shares at 677p by period end, and purchases continued into late September. The company also bought 396,052 shares at 664p from employees on 15 Sep. Both put a modest bid under a thin stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prices hold flat in 1p steps on low volume, with a 20-day realised vol of 8%. The buyback sets a floor rather than driving moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Ongoing buyback support is known. It bears only on how far the downside can run on the day.

baseline_tension: The lean (-0.03) and run-up (+0.6% over 20 days, -1.5% over 60) are essentially flat, and anchor_covered is false. The mild negative NAV lean neither agrees with nor fights a positioning signal, because there is none.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic RNS record on Investegate WAS the primary source: the Pantheon budget comparison comes from two RNS texts read side by side, and the founder sale from a TR-1. The trade press (insurance-edge, Insurance Business) only restated those RNS.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the dividend drag on NAV per share rests on public payouts, so it went from -0.3 to -0.1.
The same rule applied to Pantheon: the lower budget is public and only the mark is inference, so -0.8 became -0.6.

'Too small about the move; let history move p_up, not abs': abs_move went from 2.5 to 3.0, because NAV is the new number in the release. The low history (0.9% on both HY prints) stays in p_up at 45 rather than capping the size.
Positioning is the thing to beat: the founder sale was disclosed 12 days ago and the price has risen since, so -0.2 became -0.1.
Narrow proxy: ATC acquisition momentum as a read on its mark is a proxy, so +0.2 became +0.15.
